Cha Ca
Oct 2017
Located at road junction of Hoa Ma and Ngo Thi Nhậm Road. You will noticed a beautiful fish sculpture on the side wall just before the restaurant. Go before early to avoid the lunch time crowd.
The famous Cha Ca is fried with drill and sliced spring onion and eaten with different dipping.
I did not try the fermented shrimp dipping which need an acquired taste buds.
Clean air-conditioned interior with helpful staff.
This Kinh Ky restaurant is definitely a better place to try Cha Ca(fried fish on a pan).

Lovely dinner marred by rushed exit
Mar 2017 • Family
On my last night in Hanoi we decided to enjoy the traditional fried fish dinner with delicious fresh greens, which is cooked by the wait staff. All was well until we had finished our dinner. At that time two wait staff began cleaning up around us as we were finishing our conversation. I asked if it were okay to remain seated and received a nod from the waitress. However, the staff continued to reset the table .... new dishes, napkins, etc. as we sat there. We were confused and definitely annoyed by this behavior. It felt so unnecessary since there were plenty of tables ready of any newly arriving diners. We hope other guests are not subject to this behavior in the future.

Great local dish
Mar 2017 • Friends
I tried cha ca for the first time at Kinh Ky's Hoa Ma outlet, as we were staying at the Sunway Hotel (10 mins easy walk). Beautiful, bright yellow building - can't miss it. 

The smells were the first to tempt me, and when they brought over our pan of fried snakehead fish, huge bowl of spring onions and dill, plus accouterments, I was hooked. 

The fish was cut into bite sized pieces and deep-fried with tumeric and salt. We tossed the greens in to cook under the fish, and ate that as a topping to the small parcels of vermicelli rice noodles and salty-tangy dressing provided as the base of the cha ca meal. Absolutely delightful, especially if you enjoy do-it-yourself type meals. 

The snakehead fish was an interesting experience. Being a freshwater fish, it tasted similar to carp, catfish or eel, but the muddy tones were rather faint and muted. I am a total fan, though - love at first bite. 

It was a little difficult communicating with the staff at the Hoa Ma outlet, as only the manager spoke English (and he was busy managing the huge lunch crowd), but we managed to get by with general hand gestures and pointing. 

Definitely recommend the cha ca here; we had a fabulous lunch, and the building and decor were delightfully quaint.
